guarantees.claim: When add_state_out_sel equals ADD_SO_ZERO or any value not matching ADD_SO_IV or ADD_SO_DIP, add_state_out is driven to all zeros.
guarantees.cond: add_state_out_sel == ADD_SO_ZERO or not (ADD_SO_IV or ADD_SO_DIP)

guarantees.claim: When add_state_out_sel equals ADD_SO_IV, add_state_out is assigned the transposed value of iv_q: aes_transpose(iv_q).
When add_state_out_sel equals ADD_SO_DIP, add_state_out is assigned the transposed value of data_in_prev_q: aes_transpose(data_in_prev_q).

assumptions.claim: The select signal add_state_out_sel is always driven to one of the three defined values: ADD_SO_ZERO, ADD_SO_IV, or ADD_SO_DIP.
assumptions.cond: always when this mux is active
assumptions.risk: If an undefined value appears, the block silently outputs zero instead of the intended IV or DIP data, potentially corrupting AES state and weakening security.

assumptions.claim: When add_state_out_sel selects ADD_SO_IV, iv_q contains a valid IV value.
assumptions.risk: Using an invalid IV leads to an incorrect AES state addition, breaking encryption integrity.

assumptions.claim: When add_state_out_sel selects ADD_SO_DIP, data_in_prev_q contains valid DIP data.
assumptions.risk: Using invalid DIP data results in an erroneous state addition, compromising cipher operation.

uncertain_points.claim: The default case outputs zero for any unrecognized add_state_out_sel value without error detection or containment.
uncertain_points.cond: add_state_out_sel takes a value not equal to ADD_SO_ZERO, ADD_SO_IV, or ADD_SO_DIP
uncertain_points.risk: An illegal select caused by a fault or attack could silently force the AES state to zero, potentially enabling a chosen‑zero attack or silent data corruption.
